chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the time for prayer enters, the gates of heaven are opened for the ascent of deeds, so I love that no deed ascends before my deed, and that no one is recorded in the register before me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of performing prayer at its designated time according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the metaphysical reality that prayer times serve as celestial windows for the ascent of deeds, a concept rooted in Shia cosmology regarding the connection between the earthly and heavenly realms. He personalizes this spiritual mechanism by expressing his intense eagerness to be the first to pray, ensuring his worship ascends promptly and is recorded first in the divine register, thereby emphasizing the virtue of *sabq* (precedence) in acts of worship. This reflects the broader Shia emphasis on not only the validity but also the excellence and timeliness of obligatory acts as a means of drawing closer to God.
